label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
Hi Mikaela, happy to give you the real version. You helped us heaps when Dave did his shoulder, so it's the least I can do.

We've got 290 cows, mostly 3-way crossbreds. We started on 21 Sept, after mating had started. We milk at 5.15 every morning, and skip the arvo on Tues, Thurs and Sat, plus Sunday arvo. So that's 4 once-a-days a week.

**Production:** we're down about 6% on the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. The rep had told us to expect 8-10, so we came in better than he said, but it's still a real drop and it's only one spring of numbers.

**Cells:** they did jump, from about 110k to around 180k over the first 3 weeks. They're back to about 135k now. So not mental, but you'll see it go up before it settles, and I wouldn't want you surprised by that.

**The bad bit:** we had a heifer get mastitis on a skipped arvo and I didn't spot it till the next morning. She lost a quarter. That one's on us, and it's the main thing I'd warn you about. You have to be right on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days, because if you get lazy it bites you. You can't just let the day go by and assume everything's fine.

**The good stuff:** lameness is way down. We've got 4 on the lame list now against 11 this time last year, and our long walk to the back paddocks is 1.8km, so I reckon fewer walks to the shed is helping there. The cows also came round quicker than I thought. We had about 4 days of bellowing at the gate and then they were fine.

The hours made the biggest difference for us though. The first Sunday arvo we skipped, Dave and I went to Hamilton to see the grandkids. It was our first Sunday off in spring in 20-odd years. And Kieran, our 2IC, said it's the first spring he hasn't wanted to quit by October. You mentioned your young fella is already talking about leaving, so that might matter to you. If Tom's knees are bad, I reckon the arvos off will help him more than anything else you could change.

Honestly I wouldn't go back. For me the hours alone are worth the 6%. But that's us, and you know your own farm and your own people. Just go in knowing about the cells, the production hit and the extra attention you need to pay on the skip days.

If you want to see how it works in practice, come have a look at our shed rosters and numbers at the field day at Kerrisons on the 19th. I'll have it all with me and you can ask whatever you like.

Or just ring me if you'd rather, it's easier than texting. My thumbs are useless!

Bev
